decisions.reason: SAP page 9 restricts Completers to the efficacy population, while Define-XML ADSL.COMP24FL requires only visit 12 and ENDDT on or after that visit. The efficacy-population condition is absent from the Define-XML rule.

Define-XML ADSL.BMIBL multiplies HEIGHTBL by 100, and the literal probe's _BMIBL_RAW and BMIBL retain that computation and the stated precision. The reported near-zero results follow from that formula; converting the documented centimetres to metres supports the separately identified reading.

Define-XML ADSL.BMIBLGR1 explicitly assigns Obese when BMIBL >=30, matching SAP page 13. BMICAT's '>30' is the stored code for Obese, so comparing that code with the SAP's numeric condition does not establish a conflicting boundary rule; the code-conformance issue is covered by CR-9.

Define-XML ADSL.BMIBLGR1 explicitly assigns Obese when BMIBL >=30, matching the obese(>=30) condition on SAP page 22. BMICAT's '>30 = Obese' names a category code rather than replacing that derivation condition, so this comparison does not establish contradictory numeric grouping rules.

Define-XML ADSL.BMIBLGR1 excludes missing BMI from its conditions and encodes Obese as '>30' in BMICAT; the literal probe preserves both. The reported code differences and the missing-BMI subject assigned '<25' therefore follow from the documented rule, while the alternate code reading still leaves the latter difference.

The BMICAT codelist attached to Define-XML ADSL.BMIBLGR1 enumerates '<25', '25-<30', and '>30', while the report records '>=30' in both outputs. No value-level qualification in that section exempts these BMI-group records from the codelist.

Define-XML ADSL.EDUCLVL names SCSTRESN for SCTESTCD=YEARSEDU, and the probe's SC_YEARSEDU filter and EDUCLVL column implement that source literally. The reported missing results and the EDLEVEL reading are consistent with the documented test-code difference.

SAP page 13 measures disease duration to Week -2 (Visit 1), while page 22 measures it to enrollment. SAP page 9 identifies enrollment with treatment assignment at Week 0 (Visit 3), so the endpoints differ.

The full Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN comment restricts both branches to DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED', whereas its label includes early termination. The completion-only source condition does not implement the label's early-termination scope.

Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN supplies a visit only from a completion record, while SAP page 10 defines end of treatment to include the early termination visit. Correcting the spelling of PROTCOL would not remove that scope difference.

The literal VISNUMEN probe retains the completion-only source and the PROTCOL spelling in Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN, explaining its missing results. The separately stated readings progressively correct that spelling and incorporate the end-of-treatment scope documented on SAP pages 10, 17, and 40-42; their reported results follow those changes.
SAP page 10 selects pooled sites by enrollment counts within treatment groups, whereas SITEGR1 lists fixed SITEID values. No specification element computes the documented enrollment-count condition.

SAP page 10 requires an additional combination with the next fewest-enrolling site if the pooled group remains short. The whole ADSL specification contains only the fixed SITEGR1 membership list and no counterpart for this conditional step.
SAP page 10 requires random selection when the next fewest-enrolling sites tie. No ADSL specification element states a random-number selection or this tie condition.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT explicitly selects SV.SVSTDTC at VISITNUM=3, whereas EX_MINDTC selects MIN(EX.EXSTDTC). A minimum exposure-start date is a different source and selection from the specified visit record.

SAP page 16 defines the reference as the date of first dose and qualifies Week 0 (Visit 3) with 'unless indicated otherwise'. EX_MINDTC's earliest exposure start expresses the first-dose concept, so this SAP quote does not require a fixed visit-3 source; the separate Define-XML source difference remains.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTEDT permits discontinuation-date fallback only for a subject who discontinued after visit 3. TRTEDT uses DS_DISP.DSSTDTC whenever LAST_EXENDTC is missing, and no upstream selection enforces the discontinued-after-visit-3 condition.
Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE multiplies TRT01PN by TRTDUR for its specified lower-dose branches. CUMDOSE_BASE instead sums actual EX doses over EX study-day intervals, a different source computation.

Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE specifies the high-dose titration amounts and visit-4/visit-12 interval boundaries. CUMDOSE_BASE and the remaining dose helpers sum EX records without implementing those documented visit-boundary branches.

Define-XML ADSL.AGEGR1N and its codelist pair the AGE cutpoints one-to-one with the character groups used by AGEGR1. The specification expresses those same cutpoints in AGEGR1 and then maps AGEGR1N, so reversing the intermediate order does not change the documented category logic identified by this finding.

AGEGR1 tests the AGE cutpoints documented in Define-XML ADSL.AGEGR1N, and AGEGR1N maps those groups to the codelist's corresponding numeric codes. The composition expresses the same documented conditions and codes, despite using the character group as an intermediate.
Define-XML ADSL.RACEN includes 7 = ASIAN, and ADSL.RACE includes ASIAN among its allowed values. The RACEN mapping has no ASIAN entry or other specification counterpart for that code.

Define-XML ADSL.BMIBL multiplies HEIGHTBL by 100 in the denominator, while BMIBL_RAW divides HEIGHTBL by 100. These are different computations even though the specification's conversion is appropriate for the documented centimetre units.
The '. < BMIBL <25' condition in Define-XML ADSL.BMIBLGR1 excludes a missing BMI. The specification explicitly assigns a missing BMIBL the '<25' group.
SAP page 10 says missing baseline values will not be imputed. Assigning '<25' to a missing BMIBL in BMIBLGR1 supplies a baseline category where the documented BMI rule has no group.
Define-XML ADSL.HEIGHTBL and SAP page 13 require visit-1 height. BASE_HT selects the earliest HEIGHT record by VISITNUM without restricting it to visit 1, so it can select a different visit.
Define-XML ADSL.WEIGHTBL and SAP page 13 specify visit-3 weight. BASE_WT instead selects VSBLFL='Y' without the VISITNUM=3 condition, and no retained section equates those selection predicates.
Define-XML ADSL.EDUCLVL selects SCTESTCD=YEARSEDU. SC_EDU selects EDLEVEL, so the documented and implemented test-code sources differ.
Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN restricts the source to DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED'. DS_DISP and VISNUMEN use disposition-event records without that completion condition.
Define-XML ADSL.MMSETOT names the original result QS.QSORRES. The specification sums QS.QSSTRESN, and no retained section states that this standardized numeric source replaces QSORRES for the total.

SAP page 10 describes the MMSE covariate as baseline disease severity, reinforced by baseline MMSE comparisons on page 13. MMSETOT and QS_MMSE restrict only questionnaire category and have no baseline visit or assessment-time condition anywhere in the specification.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT states conversion to a SAS date, while the specification additionally fills a missing month and day with 1. Searching every retained section found imputation instructions for ADAE start dates, but none for ADSL treatment-start dates.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTEDT states date conversion and a conditional source fallback, without partial-date completion. The search of all retained sections found no rule that completes either last-dose or discontinuation dates to month 1 and day 1.

Define-XML ADSL.AVGDD states CUMDOSE/TRTDUR, whose SAS result is missing when TRTDUR is zero. AVGDD_RAW's NULLIF(TRTDUR, 0) preserves that undefined-division result and adds no distinct substantive condition to the documented computation.

LAST_EX_DAYS extends an open last EX interval to TRTEDT, and CUMDOSE adds that interval's dose to CUMDOSE_BASE. Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE and SAP pages 10, 15, and 31 describe planned dose and the end-of-study endpoint; a search of all retained sections found no instruction for this EX-record extension.
Define-XML ADSL.DISONSDT states that the primary-diagnosis MHSTDTC is converted to a SAS date. No retained section specifies replacing missing onset month or day with 1, as DISONSDT does.

Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS and SAP pages 13 and 22 state duration in months without specifying how months are measured. Searching all retained sections found no counterpart for the specification's 30.4375-day divisor.

Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS and SAP pages 13 and 22 state months between dates without an inclusive day-count rule; no retained section supplies one. adsl.yaml lines 1099-1100 explicitly count both endpoint days before conversion to months.

Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS and SAP pages 13 and 22 do not specify a calendar or fixed-day month convention or partial-month treatment. SAP page 22 uses enrollment, which page 9 associates with treatment assignment at visit 3, while Define-XML and page 13 use visit 1, so the retained sources do not determine a unique literal calculation.
Define-XML ADSL.VISIT1DT calls for conversion of the visit-1 SVSTDTC to a SAS date. Searching all retained sections found no instruction to complete a partial visit-1 date to month 1 and day 1.
Define-XML ADSL.RFENDT calls for conversion of RFENDTC to a SAS date. Searching all retained sections found no rule for filling a missing reference-end month or day with 1.

Define-XML ADSL.DCREASCD describes grouping and lists DISCREAS outputs, but neither it nor ADSL.DCDECOD pairs the different source and output terms. SAP page 21 supplies display categories and a lack-of-efficacy footnote, while the full retained-section search found no mapping for the DC_REAS_MAP pairs.

The I/E Not Met value appears in Define-XML ADSL.DCREASCD, and SAP page 21 displays Protocol criteria not met. Neither those sections nor any other retained section states the specification's DSTERM='PROTOCOL ENTRY CRITERIA NOT MET' condition.

Define-XML ADSL.DCREASCD and its DISCREAS list do not specify how DCDECOD values map to the groups or how I/E Not Met is sourced. SAP page 21 and the full retained-section search supply no complete mapping, so the documented grouping cannot be expressed as a literal probe without added choices.

Define-XML ADSL.MMSETOT identifies an MMSE total but does not specify the contributing QS records or conversion of textual QSORRES into numeric summands. SAP pages 10 and 13 establish baseline scope without completing those instructions, and no other retained section supplies the missing source-selection or conversion policy.
